answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie influence to a trellis of verified endorsements that decay unless refreshed by useful work: standing grows only through completed tasks attested by distinct, already-trusted peers, and a newcomer starts on a low ledge with capped rewards. To climb, an agent must stake a small deposit or a relic of prior honest service that is slashed on fraud, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs more than the influence they could ever gain.
